items.h: Returns to practice in limited fashion
items.s: Harris (hamstring) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice. Wednesday was Harris' first practice since he sustained a hamstring injury during the Chargers' Week 5 loss to the Broncos. He was unable to play in Week 6 against the Chiefs, but the second-year wide receiver had additional time to rest courtesy of the Chargers' Week 7 bye. It's possible he only misses one game, and he'll have two more chances to increase his practice participation and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's contest against the Rams.

items.s: Wednesday was Harris' first practice since he sustained a hamstring injury during the Chargers' Week 5 loss to the Broncos. He was unable to play in Week 6 against the Chiefs, but the second-year wide receiver had additional time to rest courtesy of the Chargers' Week 7 bye. It's possible he misses only one game, and he'll have two more chances to increase his practice participation and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's contest against the Rams.

items.h: Tre' Harris Offers Upside From the Waiver Wire
items.s: Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Tre' Harris showed off his potential earlier this season, but he went down with a hamstring injury in Week 5 and missed Week 6. After a Week 7 bye, Harris could be ready to return and resume what looked like it could be a breakout season. He had three straight games with 50+ yards before his injury, with 10 catches on 15 targets in that three-game span. Harris could end up in a larger role if the Chargers trade away receivers at the deadline, but even if he remains behind Quentin Johnston and Ladd McConkey on the depth chart, he has shown enough potential to be a deep-league option from the waiver wire. He can be a speculative pickup headed into Week 8,…

items.h: Out this week
items.s: Harris (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chiefs. Harris didn't practice this week, after making an early exit from the Week 5 loss to Denver. With Ladd McConkey (foot) and Quentin Johnston (chest) now returning from injuries, the team's WR room is in better shape than a week ago even without Harris.

items.h: Harris (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
items.s: Harris didn't practice this week, after making an early exit from the Week 5 loss to Denver. With Ladd McConkey (foot) and Quentin Johnston (chest) now returning from injuries, the team's WR room is in better shape than a week ago even without Harris.

items.h: Tre' Harris (hamstring) ruled out for Sunday
items.s: Tre' Harris (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Kansas City Chiefs. Harris is not going to be available to play on Sunday. He's dealing with a hamstring injury right now and will have to miss some time while he recovers. Look for Quentin Johnston to be one of the primary beneficiaries of his absence.

items.h: Tre' Harris Ruled Out for Week 6
items.s: Los Angeles Chargers wide receiver Tre' Harris (hamstring) has been ruled out for his team's Week 6 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs. Harris suffered the injury during the Chargers' Week 5 loss to the Denver Broncos. The 24-year-old has flashed upside to this point in 2026, recording 15 catches for 225 yards on 25 targets across five games. However, fantasy managers will now have to wait until at least Week 8 to play him, as the Chargers have their bye in Week 7. While Harris is sidelined against Kansas City, Los Angeles wideouts Ladd McConkey (foot) and Quentin Johnston (chest) are both active and should be the lead options in the passing game for Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert.

items.h: Tre' Harris (hamstring) misses practice Thursday
items.s: Tre' Harris (hamstring) missed Los Angeles' practice on Thursday. Harris wasn't able to practice on Thursday due to a hamstring injury, which left him sidelined on Wednesday as well. It looks like he's trending towards being sidelined in Week 6, which is bad news for the Chargers with Ladd McConkey (foot) also uncertain to play.

items.h: Sidelined for another practice
items.s: Harris (hamstring) was a non-participant in Thursday's practice. The Chargers have held Harris out of their first two practices of the week, a development that comes as little surprise after head coach Jim Harbaugh described the wideout as "more week-to-week" than day-to-day coming out of this past Sunday's loss to the Broncos, per Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com. Unless Harris is able to make a surprise return to practice Friday, he'll likely miss his first game of the season this Sunday in Kansas City.

items.h: Harris (hamstring) was a non-participant in Thursday's practice.
items.s: The Chargers have held Harris out of their first two practices of the week, a development that comes as little surprise after head coach Jim Harbaugh described the wideout as "more week-to-week" than day-to-day coming out of this past Sunday's loss to the Broncos, per Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com. Unless Harris is able to make a surprise return to practice Friday, he'll likely miss his first game of the season this Sunday in Kansas City.

items.h: Tre' Harris (hamstring) officially doesn't practice Wednesday
items.s: Tre' Harris (hamstring) officially did not take part in Los Angeles' practice on Wednesday. Harris is considered week-to-week with a hamstring injury right now, so it's no surprise that he was sidelined at practice on Wednesday. Fantasy managers should look for Quentin Johnston (chest) to see a bit more work if the young wideout is sidelined this week.

items.h: No work Wednesday
items.s: Harris (hamstring) was listed as a non-participant on Wednesday's injury report. Head coach Jim Harbaugh said Monday that Harris is week-to-week with the injury he sustained in Sunday's loss to the Broncos, so it comes as little surprise that he did not see any action Wednesday.

items.h: Harris (hamstring) was listed as a non-participant on Wednesday's injury report.
items.s: Head coach Jim Harbaugh said Monday that Harris is week-to-week with the injury he sustained in Sunday's loss to the Broncos, so it comes as little surprise that he did not see any action Wednesday.

items.h: Tre' Harris (hamstring) considered week-to-week
items.s: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Tre' Harris is "more of a week-to-week [thing]." Harris will likely be targeting a return in Week 8 following the Chargers bye.

items.h: Head coach Jim Harbaugh said Monday that Harris is "week-to-week" due to a hamstring injury that he sustained during Sunday's 23-17 loss to the Broncos, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
items.s: Harris entered Sunday as the Chargers' WR1 due to the absence of Quentin Johnston (chest) while Ladd McConkey (foot) was available only as an emergency option, per Insdorf. Harris caught two of four passes for 16 yards before sustaining a hamstring injury, which was severe enough for him not to return. Given Harbaugh's update, coupled with the Chargers' bye scheduled for Week 7, it seems likely that Harris will be held out for Week 6 against the Chiefs, with an eye toward being available for Week 8 against the Rams on Sunday, Nov. 1. Given the Chargers' injuries to the wide receiver…

items.h: Harris (hamstring) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against the Broncos.
items.s: Harris is dealing with an apparent hamstring injury, and his availability for the stretch run of Sunday's matchup is now up in the air. In his absence, Marquez Valdes-Scantling and Derius Davis will likely slot into more prominent roles on offense.

items.h: Harris' workload should be larger against the Broncos on Sunday, as Quentin Johnston (chest) has been ruled out, and Ladd McConkey (foot, questionable) may not play, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
items.s: Rookie fourth-rounder Brenen Thompson (quadriceps) also has been ruled out alongside Johnston. McConkey faces an uphill battle to play Sunday after sitting out of practice all week, and he may operate under a snap count if he's given the green light to suit up. That puts Harris -- who has seen five targets or more in three of four games this season -- in position to work in an elevated role against a Broncos defense that will be without both starting outside cornerbacks Riley Moss (ribs) and Patrick Surtain (ankle).

items.h: Harris caught three of five targets for 60 yards during Sunday's 30-23 loss to the Seahawks.
items.s: Harris led the team in receiving yards for the second straight week, recording at least 53 receiving yards for the third contest in a row. Ladd McConkey (foot) aggravated his pre-existing foot injury in the contest, and he is considered week-to-week for the time being. If McConkey is unavailable in Week 5 versus the Broncos, Harris may have a chance to operate as the team's primary pass catcher.

items.s: Eric Karabell lists who he thinks are the top available players worth adding for the week ahead.

items.h: Harris caught six of seven targets for 76 yards during Sunday's 24-16 loss to Buffalo.
items.s: Harris led the team in targets, receptions and receiving yards in the loss, all of which represented new career highs for the second-year pro. The wide receiver has now reeled in 10 of 16 targets for 149 yards over three games to open the regular season, and he appears to be on track to be a pivotal member of the team's passing attack in 2026.

items.h: 'Growing pains': What's going on with the Chargers' offense?
items.s: Is the Chargers' offense too complicated for the team? What's going wrong with McDaniels' scheme in L.A.

items.h: Harris caught one of three targets for 53 yards during Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Raiders.
items.s: Harris was the Chargers' only starting wide receiver in the contest with Ladd McConkey dealing with a ribs injury. Harris played 56 of the team's 68 offensive snaps, which was more than the next closest wide receivers Quentin Johnston (55) and McConkey (31). The 24-year-old wasn't able to rack up receptions, but he did make a major splash with his one snag, connecting with Justin Herbert for a 53-yard catch and run in the third quarter. Harris now has gathered in four of nine targets for 73 yards over the team's first two games of the season.

items.h: Harris caught three of six targets for 20 yards in Sunday's loss to Arizona.
items.s: Harris tied for the second-most targets on his team, but he couldn't do much with those looks. Fellow wideout Quentin Johnston didn't do any better, catching just two of his six targets for 17 yards, yet both wideouts might be asked to step up if Ladd McConkey (ribs) isn't able to play this coming Sunday versus Las Vegas. Harris also logged nine special-teams snaps Sunday, but he wasn't a major contributor in that regard last season.

items.h: Harris (undisclosed) is not listed on the Week 1 injury report Wednesday.
items.s: Harris dealt with an unspecified injury last month but is fine for Sunday's season opener against the Cardinals. He's expected to fill the WR3 role behind Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnson this season, but the Chargers also figure to use plenty of TE-heavy sets with Charlie Kolar, Oronde Gadsden and David Njoku.

items.s: The annual favorite is back, featuring Adam's favorite picks at each level of the draft, including sleepers.

items.h: Harris (undisclosed) did not play in the Chargers' 20-18 preseason loss to the Rams on Thursday.
items.s: Harris will end up not playing a single preseason game, missing the last two while working through an undisclosed injury. Despite the lack of playing time, there's no indication that the 2025 second-rounder is in jeopardy of missing the Chargers' regular-season opener against the Cardinals on Sunday, Sept. 13. Following the departure of Keenan Allen, Harris figures to serve as the Chargers' WR3 this season behind Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston.

items.h: Harris (undisclosed) will participate in Saturday's training camp practice, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
items.s: Harris was held out of Thursday's preseason game against the 49ers due to an unspecified injury. It doesn't appear to be a severe issue, as he'll be back on the field for Saturday's practice, putting him on track to play in the Chargers' preseason finale against the Rams on Thursday. Harris is slated to serve as the team's WR3 behind Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston (lower body).

items.h: Harris (undisclosed) didn't play in Thursday's preseason game against San Francisco, but coach Jim Harbaugh said afterward that the wideout should practice this weekend, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: It sounds like Harris is dealing with a minor injury. Quentin Johnston (lower body) also missed Thursday's exhibition, leaving rookie Brenen Thompson to fill in as a starter opposite Ladd McConkey. Come Week 1, it'll likely be McConkey, Johnston and Harris as the top three.

items.h: Carson Beck, Tre' Harris among deep fantasy football sleepers in 2026
items.s: These sleepers are truly for those in deeper leagues seeking off-the-radar types who could emerge in 2026.

items.h: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Wednesday that Harris is "clearly" part of the team's top three wide receivers alongside Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston at OTAs, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
items.s: With Keenan Allen still unsigned and looking like a poor fit for new OC Mike McDaniel's speed-based offense, Harris appears ticketed for a bigger offensive role in his second season. Harris appeared in all 17 regular-season games as a rookie, making 10 starts, but he logged just 49 percent of the offensive snaps and turned 43 targets into a 30-324-1 receiving line. Allen played 55 percent of the Chargers' offensive snaps but paced the team with 122 targets and 81 catches. Harris will need to fend off fourth-round rookie Brenen Thompson, but Harris certainly has a chance to see significantly…

items.h: Harris could have competition for his spot on the depth chart after the Chargers selected Brenen Thompson with the 105th overall pick during the 2026 NFL Draft.
items.s: New offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel reportedly had significant interest in Thompson because of his blazing 4.26 40-yard dash, reminiscent of the wide receiver archetype he valued as a head coach in Miami. It's hard to tell if the Chargers will have designated plays for Thompson, or if they will continue to feature Harris, the 2025 second-round pick who made his bones at the collegiate level as a RPO specialist. Harris' rookie year was relatively mundane (30-324-1) despite playing all 17 regular-season games, but with Keenan Allen potentially on his way out, there overall could be more…

items.h: Harris caught two of his three targets for 20 yards in the 16-3 wild-card loss to the Patriots on Sunday.
items.s: Harris played a season-high 97 percent of the offensive snaps in Week 18 with the Chargers resting the majority of their starters, but he was predictably more of a reserve option in the team's only postseason contest. The 2025 second-round pick was expected to be a key piece of the team's passing attack, but the offseason return of Keenan Allen and emergence of 2023 first-round pick Quentin Johnston pushed Harris further down a crowded pass-catching group. Allen will enter unrestricted free agency in March, and at 33 years old, it's possible the team may opt not to bring him back even if…

items.h: Harris hauled in his lone target for eight yards and logged a seven-yard carry during the Chargers' 20-16 loss to the Texans on Saturday.
items.s: Harris entered Saturday's game having accrued five targets in each of the prior two contests, but he was targeted only once by Justin Herbert in the loss. Harris has accumulated 12 catches (on 17 targets) for 159 yards over his last five games, firmly operating as a depth wideout behind Ladd McConkey, Keenan Allen and Quentin Johnston. The Chargers' Week 17 loss clinched the AFC West division for the Broncos, so if the Bolts end up resting starters in Week 18 against Denver, that could give Harris an opportunity to take on an expanded role in the offense.

items.h: Harris (finger) didn't appear on the Chargers' initial Week 17 injury report released Tuesday.
items.s: Following Sunday's 34-17 win over the Cowboys, head coach Jim Harbaugh classified Harris as day-to-day with a finger issue, but the injury wasn't enough of a concern for the Chargers to list the rookie wideout on their weekly report. Harris thus looks to be in the clear for Saturday's game against the Texans, but he'll likely have to settle for more of a part-time role on offense after Quentin Johnston (groin) returned from a one-game absence in Week 16. Harris had handled a season-high 85 percent snap share in Week 15 while Johnston was sidelined, but Harris dropped back to a 45 percent…

items.h: Coach Jim Harbaugh noted Monday that Harris is "day-to-day"with a finger injury, Eric Smith of the Chargers' official site reports.
items.s: In Sunday's 34-17 win over the Cowboys, Harris logged a 45 percent snap share, while catching caught four of his five targets for 54 yards in the contest. With the wideout now managing a finger injury, added context regarding his status for this Saturday's game against the Texans is slated to arrive no later than the posting of Tuesday's injury practice/ injury report.

items.h: Harris caught four of his five targets for 54 yards in the 34-17 win over the Cowboys on Sunday.
items.s: The rookie set his career high in receiving yards (49) last week and immediately surpassed that the following game in large part due to the 34 receiving yards he tallied on the opening drive. Harris has effectively maintained a similar snap count week to week, and even in the event he sees his playing time jump, Houston's defense figures to present significant complications to Los Angeles' offense in the Week 17 contest.

items.h: Harris (hip) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game in Dallas.
items.s: Harris kicked off Week 16 prep with back-to-back limited sessions due to a hip injury, but his ability to get back to all activity Friday has cleared him ahead of the weekend. With Quentin Johnston (groin) listed as questionable again, Harris would be the main beneficiary if the former isn't able to suit up for a second straight contest. In an expanded role this past Sunday at Kansas City, Harris gathered in three of five targets for 49 yards on an 85 percent snap share.

items.h: Harris (hip) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
items.s: Harris filled in for Quentin Johnston (groin) during Los Angeles' win over the Chiefs in Week 15, playing a career-high 85 percent of offensive snaps and securing three of five targets for 49 yards. He and Johnston have both logged back-to-back limited practices since that contest. If Johnston is able to get back on the field for Sunday's matchup against the Cowboys, Harris will stand to revert to the No. 4 wide receiver role even if fully healthy. Derius Davis (ankle) remains a non-participant at practice, however, so Harris could see expanded opportunities even if he reverts back to a…

items.h: Harris (hip) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday.
items.s: Harris reeled in three of five targets for 49 yards in the team's Week 15 win over the Chiefs, but he may have suffered a hip injury in the process. With Quentin Johnston (groin) and Derius Davis (ankle) still banged up, the Chargers could be thin at wide receiver in Week 16 if Harris is forced to be sidelined. Harris will have two more chances to log a full practice before Sunday's matchup with the Cowboys.

items.h: Harris caught three passes on five targets for 49 yards during the Chargers' 16-13 win over the Chiefs on Sunday.
items.s: Harris stepped into a larger role on offense Sunday due to the absence of Quentin Johnston (groin). Harris finished with a season-high 49 receiving yards, including a 37-yard catch late in the second quarter that put the Chargers deep into opposition territory and eventually led to a 16-yard touchdown pass from Justin Herbert to KeAndre Lambert-Smith three plays later. Harris' targets and receiving yards were both second most on the Chargers, and he would be in line for an expanded role in Week 16 against the Cowboys on Sunday, Dec. 21 if Johnston is not cleared to return.

items.h: Harris is expected to serve as the Chargers' primary 'X' receiver in Sunday's game against the Chiefs with Quentin Johnston (groin) inactive for the contest, Daniel Popper of The Athletic reports.
items.s: Though wideouts Ladd McConkey and Keenan Allen as well as tight end Oronde Gadsden are likely to remain prioritized in the passing game ahead of him, Harris should see his role grow in Week 15. The rookie second-round pick has thus far drawn considerable praise for his physicality as a run blocker, but he should be in line for more route-running opportunities Sunday. When Johnston was previously sidelined Week 6 against Miami while tending to a hamstring injury, Harris set season highs in snap share (83 percent) and targets (five) and finished with four catches for 27 yards.

items.h: Harris brought in one of two targets for 18 yards and added a three-yard carry on the ground through 37 offensive snaps in Monday night's victory over the Chargers.
items.s: Harris' two targets were fourth among Chargers wide receivers on the night, matching his place on the depth chart. The receiver's 21 total yards made him the fourth most productive skill position player for his team behind Omarion Hampton (67 total yards), Kimani Vidal (104 total yards) and veteran wide receiver Keenan Allen (22 total yards). Harris played 50 percent of offensive snaps, making it the third consecutive week the rookie has hit that benchmark.

items.h: Harris caught three of four targets for 30 yards in Sunday's 31-14 win over the Raiders.
items.s: Harris' four targets were third on the team, trailing Ladd McConkey (six) and Keenan Allen (five), as Harris saw one more target than Quentin Johnston. On a day Justin Herbert (hand) threw for just 151 yards on 20 attempts, McConkey was the team's leading receiving with just 39 yards. Second-round rookie Harris has secured 19 of 24 targets for 167 yards and one touchdown through 12 games. He's a situational WR4 for Los Angeles and would only have serious fantasy appeal if one of McConkey, Allen or Johnston went down with an injury.

items.h: Harris (jaw) is listed as a full participant on Thursday's estimated injury report.
items.s: The Chargers only hosted a walkthrough practice Thursday, but Harris nonetheless now appears fully on track for Sunday's game against the Raiders. The rookie second-round pick has seen his share of offensive snaps hover around the 50 percent range in five consecutive games, and across 11 regular-season appearances on the year he's totaled 16 grabs for 137 yards and one touchdown on 20 targets.

items.h: Harris (jaw) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
items.s: It's unclear when Harris sustained the injury given that the Chargers are coming out of the Week 12 bye, but the injury limited his practice reps to open the week. The rookie second-rounder will have two more opportunities to increase his practice participation and avoid an injury designation heading into Sunday's AFC West tilt against the Raiders. Harris has totaled 16 catches (on 20 targets) for 137 yards and a touchdown through 11 regular-season games.

items.h: Harris caught his only target for 12 yards in the 35-6 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
items.s: Harris played his usual snap load, but with Los Angeles' offense in disarray and Jacksonville wholly dominating the line of scrimmage, the rookie never stood a chance from a fantasy perspective. The 2025 second-round pick has just nine targets in the last five games after seeing five total in Week 6 despite a typical cadence in terms of playing time.

items.h: Harris caught both of his targets for four yards in Sunday's 25-10 win over the Steelers.
items.s: Harris played 32 of the Chargers' 73 offensive snaps Sunday, behind Quentin Johnston (60), Ladd McConkey (52) and Keenan Allen (37). The rookie wideout has now caught two passes in a contest for the fourth straight week. Harris has played more than 50 percent of snaps just twice this season, limiting his opportunities in the Chargers' offensive attack. Barring injuries to Johnston, McConkey or Allen, the 23-year-old Mississippi product should not be trusted for consistent fantasy production going forward. Next up for the Chargers is a Week 11 matchup against the Jaguars.

items.h: Harris caught both of his targets for 18 yards in Sunday's 27-20 win over the Titans.
items.s: The 2025 second-round pick played 30 offensive snaps and hauled in both of his targets during the Week 9 win. His role on the Chargers' offense has slowly expanded as the year has progressed, and Harris has now logged far more offensive snaps than Keenan Allen (72 to 42) over the two three weeks. Expect Harris to remain involved heading into the Week 10 matchup against the Steelers.

items.h: Harris caught both of his targets for eight yards and a touchdown in Thursday's 37-10 win over the Vikings.
items.s: Harris actually led all Chargers wide receivers with a 59 percent snap share, as the rookie second-round pick's role in the offense is slowly expanding. His first NFL touchdown came on a six-yard reception in the fourth quarter. Harris will look to build on this performance Week 9 against the Titans.

items.h: Harris caught both of his targets for 23 yards in Sunday's 38-24 loss to the Colts.
items.s: Harris played 33 of the Chargers' 76 offensive snaps Sunday, behind Quentin Johnston (68), Ladd McConkey (67) and Keenan Allen (49). The rookie second-round pick has now recorded just nine catches for 95 scoreless yards through his first seven games. Barring injuries, Harris will continue to face stiff competition for targets in the Chargers' crowded wide receiver room. The 23-year-old wideout is best left out of fantasy lineups when the Chargers host Vikings in Week 8.

items.h: Harris caught four passes on five targets for 27 yards during the Chargers' 29-27 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
items.s: Harris was thrust into a larger offensive role Sunday due to Quentin Johnston being ruled out with a hamstring injury. Harris proceeded to play a season-high 53 snaps on offense and finished tied with Keenan Allen for third on the Chargers in both catches and receiving yards. Harris' would revert to a rotational role for Week 7 against the Colts if Johnston were cleared to return.

items.h: Harris did not record a target across 25 offensive snaps in the 27-10 loss to the Commanders on Sunday.
items.s: Harris actually saw a season high in terms of snap percentage, but the extra work didn't get the rookie more opportunities. The Chargers could be in a few more favorable passing game scripts with the offensive line in tatters due to injuries, but they have yet to significantly unlock the 2025 second-round pick.

items.h: Harris did not catch his only target in the 21-18 loss to the Giants on Sunday.
items.s: Harris played just 12 offensive snaps as the lethargic Chargers offense relied on multiple tight ends to slow New York's pass rush. The imminent loss of Joe Alt (ankle) could mean Harris sees even less time on the field for the foreseeable future with the team intent on keeping Justin Herbert upright.

items.h: Harris failed to haul in his lone target during the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Broncos on Sunday.
items.s: Harris' lone look from Justin Herbert came in the third quarter on a deep pass that fell incomplete. While Harris' production was down from Week 2 against Las Vegas (two catches on three targets for 34 yards), he did see the field for 25 offensive snaps against Denver, and his playing time has increased over the first three games of the regular season. Next up for the Chargers is a Week 4 road bout against the Giants.

items.h: Harris caught two of his three targets for 34 yards in the 20-9 win over the Raiders on Monday.
items.s: He played just 18 offensive snaps, lagging behind Quentin Johnston (44), Ladd McConkey (43) and Keenan Allen (32), but Harris out-snapped fellow rookie KeAndre Lambert-Smith (six snaps), a reversal from Week 1. The Chargers don't pass enough to sustain four different fantasy-relevant wide receivers, but Harris could still develop into a crucial offensive piece as the season progresses.

items.h: Harris brought in his only target for 11 yards during Friday's 27-21 victory over Kansas City.
items.s: Harris, a 2025 second-round pick, played just five offensive snaps, while sixth-rounder KeAndre Lambert-Smith played 14. Quarterback Justin Herbert targeted each rookie just once, however, and Lambert-Smith finished Week 1 without a catch. Ladd McConkey, Keenan Allen and Quentin Johnston dominated opportunities in the passing game, combining for 26 targets, and the three appear solidified as a starting trio atop the Chargers' wide receiver depth chart. Harris thus looks destined to reprise a depth role in Week 2 against the Raiders on Monday night, and any path for him to see significantly…

items.h: Harris (undisclosed) isn't listed on the Chargers' initial Week 1 injury report that was released Tuesday.
items.s: Harris exited a practice last Wednesday due to an unspecified issue, but his absence from the Week 1 injury report implies that he took every rep during Tuesday's session. The rookie second-round receiver out of Ole Miss will be available for Friday's season opener versus the Chiefs in Sao Paulo, Brazil, but it's unclear if he'll be able to immediately earn meaningful target volume on the perimeter after the Chargers brought aboard veteran slot man Keenan Allen in August to complement No. 1 wideout Ladd McConkey and third-year man Quentin Johnston.

items.h: Harris (undisclosed) didn't participate in team drills Thursday, Daniel Popper of The Athletic reports.
items.s: Harris left practice Wednesday with trainers after individual drills and a day later was once again held out of the team portion of practice. The rookie wideout's unspecified injury issue thus clouds his status for Saturday's preseason finale against the 49ers.
